recipes.name: Spinach Salad with Peaches and Pecans
ingredients_raw: 4 cups baby spinach, rinsed and dried

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Arrange pecans on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Toast in the preheated oven until pecans just begin to darken, 7 to 10 minutes. Set aside to cool.
Combine peaches, spinach, and toasted pecans in a large bowl; toss with desired amount of dressing until evenly coated.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Salad with Peaches and Pecans
raw_recipe.description: A perfect peach salad recipe with succulent fresh peaches, crisp baby spinach, toasted pecans, and tossed with poppyseed dressing for a refreshing salad.

review.reviewBody: This salad was awesome and got rave reviews from the ultra picky husband! The only things I changed were adding fresh parmesean cheese and I drizzled honey over the pecans before baking. Also, the 1/4 cup of poppy sead dressing seemed to be too much and made the spinach leafs a little soggy, so I had to add a cup more spinach. So you might want to add dressing to taste instead of pouring the whole 1/4 cup in like I did.

I was looking for a full-meal salad, so just drizzled some boneless, skinless chicken breast with the poppyseed salad dressing and threw that on the George Foreman to add to the salad. Delicious! I also kept the peach skins on (washed, of course) which added even more texture. This beautiful salad tasted even better the next day with only some canned chicken (I think the peaches had sweetened even more). For leftovers' sake, I'd keep the dressing off until serving so the spinach doesn't wilt. Thanks!

No fresh peaches yet; so I used oranges. I made a No Salt Vinaigrette from this site instead of the poppyseed dressing suggested, served it on the side for individual tastes. Topped it with homemade Cinnamon Crouton, also from this site. We enjoyed this very much; can't wait to make it using fresh peaches. Thanks for posting, Robin Durawa.

This recipe was quite the hitat my dinner party! I had to deal with off-season flavorless peaches so after I cut them up I sprinkled a bit of sugar and almond flavoring on them and let them sit for about 15 minutes. Worked VERY well.

I made this for a picnic last night. Soooo easy, yes I made a few minor changes - used 1/2 spinach and 1/2 arugula. Then what seemed to be the wow factor was adding some crumbled plain goat cheese when combining all ingredients. Felt so healthy especially with the Colorado peaches that have just arrived I Minnesota.will definitely make again

This was a great salad. I used mixed baby greens and added fresh blueberries along with the peaches. I also added grated Asiago cheese, chives, and freshly ground black pepper. I used poppyseed dressing by Paula from this site and spruced up the dressing by adding a little more vinegar, dry mustard, and grated sweet onion. I put the dressing on the salad to taste instead of all at once. Lastly, I added some grilled chicken. Delicious.

Made it for a Ladies-Sunday Alta Tennis Match. 
Anyone playing tennis in the ATL Area knows the Food provided is almost as important as winning the match. LOL!! ??????
That day -the salad along with me a my tennis partner were ... “Big Hitters” - “Aced it” - “Winners!”
Making the Salad for my Family tomorrow. 
Plan to add Grilled Chicken & like the Parmesan Cheese suggestion. 
YUMMY!

Excellent salad - will definitely make again. This was so good, we made it our main course! The only change I made was to the pecans - it was too hot to turn the oven on, so I put them in the salad raw, and they were delicious.

Nice combo and easy salad to make. This can also be made for the fall by adding a few dried tart cherries, some almond slices and maybe bit's of cranberry goat cheese. If fresh peaches are other available use jarred places but drain well. Also you can use different greens. Easy and good compliment to any dinner.

After reading reviews I have changed a few things in the recipe and loved the result! I made it with mango, added feta, grilled chicken breast and finely chopped red onion. Also, I am not a great fan of dressings, so I just used some fresh lemon juice, salt and pepper. Great dinner.

This salad is easy to make but tastes like a specialty salad. It was a hit with our entire extended family! We made it the second time for a church picnic but this time put in the spinach, then the peaches, then the nuts WITHOUT MIXING so that all the heavy bits don't settle to the bottom before we got there. Upon arrival we added the dressing then lightly tossed it. Over 3,000 people have made this and not a one made their own custom version. That just shows how perfect this salad is as it stands.
Tomatoes, feta, crasins, egg, red onion, spinach, poppy seed dressing
I love this recipe . Added strawberries for color. Any fruits will work.
this was very refreshing salad!
I made this salad today and appreciated the simple list of ingredients. It was especially refreshing because of the 95 degree weather today. It a keeper.
My family absolutely loved it! We followed most of the recipe as printed only exception, we crushed the pecans. Yummy, yummy!
I used Mandarin oranges instead of Peaches and it was great.
Wonderful!
Delicious. Great summer salad.
I I used feta cheese, great salad!
